SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: CONNECTED TEXT AND FLUENCY
Subject: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Connected text and fluency helps you succeed in ENGLISH ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: CONNECTED TEXT AND FLUENCY
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Read about thirty (30) words school walls, posters and bill decidable words could be given to accurately per minute for boards in the surrounding support them . fluency, environment

What this means
In this part you learn to read about thirty (30) words school walls, posters and bill decidable words could be given to accurately per minute for boards in the surrounding support them . fluency, environment. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read about thirty (30) words school walls, posters and bill decidable words could be given to accurately per minute for boards in the surrounding support them . fluency, environment.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Connected text and fluency”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read about thirty (30) words school walls, posters and bill decidable words could be given to accurately per minute for boards in the surrounding support them . fluency, environment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate reading connected words for meaning

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate reading connected words for meaning. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate reading connected words for meaning.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Connected text and fluency to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate reading connected words for meaning. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Connected text and fluency is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Connected text and fluency”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: read about thirty (30) words school walls, posters and bill decidable words could be given to accurately per minute for boards in the surrounding support them . fluency, environment)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Connected text and fluency to a partner. (skill: appreciate reading connected words for meaning)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Connected text and fluency to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: read about thirty (30) words school walls, posters and bill decidable words could be given to accurately per minute for boards in the surrounding support them . fluency, environment.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate reading connected words for meaning.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Connected text and fluency from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Connected text and fluency: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 1 learner study Connected text and fluency?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

1. Know what Connected text and fluency means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: read about thirty (30) words school walls, posters and bill decidable words could be given to accurately per minute for boards in the surrounding support them . fluency, environment.
5. Be able to: appreciate reading connected words for meaning.
